model_annotations.Bulgarian: The chart illustrates how perplexity varies across different sparsity rates for two methods labeled “Per-Output” and “Per-Layer.” The horizontal axis contains the categories “Sparsity Rate,” shown as percentages ordered from 10% through 80% in 10% increments. The vertical axis is labeled “Perplexity” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks at approximately \(10^1\), \(10^2\), and \(10^3\), spanning from just below \(10^1\) up to about \(10^3\). At each sparsity rate, there are two side-by-side bars: a blue bar for “Per-Output” and an orange bar for “Per-Layer,” as indicated by the legend in the upper-left. The bars at 10%–50% sparsity are clustered near the lower end of the axis, with approximate values around 5–8 (e.g., near ~5–6 at 10% and rising to roughly ~7–8 by 50%) for both series. At 60%, the blue bar is around ~9–10 and the orange bar around ~10–11; at 70%, the blue bar is around ~20 while the orange bar is around ~35–40. At 80%, both bars extend into the hundreds, with the blue “Per-Output” bar around ~500 and the orange “Per-Layer” bar near ~900–1000. The bars are grouped by sparsity rate (not stacked), appear in the same left-to-right order as the x-axis categories, and there are no additional visual emphases such as annotations or outlines beyond the color coding and gridlines.
model_annotations.Chinese: The chart illustrates perplexity values measured at different sparsity rates for two methods, “Per-Output” and “Per-Layer,” shown as paired bars for each sparsity category. The horizontal axis contains the categories labeled “Sparsity Rate,” ordered from 10% through 80% in 10% increments. The vertical axis is labeled “Perplexity” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks at approximately \(10^1\), \(10^2\), and \(10^3\), spanning from just below \(10^1\) up to about \(10^3\). For each sparsity rate, two adjacent bars are displayed: a blue bar for Per-Output and an orange bar for Per-Layer, with no stacking; the bars are grouped by sparsity rate. At 10%–50% sparsity, both series have short bars clustered below \(10^1\) (roughly in the 5–8 range), with Per-Output around ~5–7 and Per-Layer around ~5–8 depending on the category; at 60% sparsity the bars rise to around ~9 (Per-Output) and ~10 (Per-Layer). At 70% sparsity, the blue Per-Output bar is around ~20 while the orange Per-Layer bar is around ~40. At 80% sparsity, the tallest bars appear, with Per-Output near ~500 and Per-Layer near ~900, approaching the \(10^3\) tick. The categories are presented in increasing sparsity order, and there are no additional visual emphases such as annotations or outlines beyond the legend and gridlines.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates how perplexity varies with sparsity rate for two methods labeled “Per-Output” and “Per-Layer.” The horizontal axis contains the categories “Sparsity Rate,” shown as percentages ordered from 10% through 80% in 10% increments. The vertical axis is labeled “Perplexity” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks at approximately 10, 100, and 1000 (10¹, 10², 10³), spanning from just below 10 up to about 1000. For each sparsity rate, there are two side-by-side bars: a blue bar for “Per-Output” and an orange bar for “Per-Layer,” with no stacking. At 10% sparsity, both bars are near about 5–6 perplexity; at 20% and 30% they remain around roughly 5–6; at 40% they are around ~6–7; at 50% around ~7–8; at 60% the blue bar is near ~9–10 and the orange bar near ~10–11; at 70% the blue bar is around ~20 while the orange bar is around ~35–40; and at 80% the blue bar is around ~500 while the orange bar is near ~900–1000. The bars are arranged by increasing sparsity rate (not sorted by value), and there are no additional visual emphases such as annotations or outlines beyond the legend and gridlines.
